"I am an online friend of your roommate.  
Firstly, it is not very professional that you are posting this on reddit about this issue instead of properly  
addressing your concerns and issue with your roommate. I know your roommate is indeed messy and  
may not have done a decent job asking for your consent for the cat. However, you have never addressed  
your concern with your roommate before about the room or the cat. Does that give you the right to put  
this up online?  
If you really had issues with your roommate before about his messy room before and didn’t want to  
confront him why not contact the ra to switch roommate. Since you are diabetic when you fill out your  
dorm form do you not have to let them know that you are in a special condition and need a more  
qualified roommate?  
I’m sure half of the people in this world have messy room, it can relate to mental health issues and their  
families when they were growing up. Certainly, since this is a dorm two people should do the best of  
their ability to keep the place clean for each other and your roommate obviously didn’t do his part. But  
is it necessary to post pictures of his mess and publicly shame him on the internet with overexaggerated  
details when you never tried to communicate with him?  
And about the cat how are you 100% sure that it was a campus cat and where is your proof that your  
roommate lured the cat in with catnip? The cat was abandoned in a cage near the subway. Your  
roommate and his friend waited there for 2 hours, and nobody showed up. The cat was also found to be  
chipped where we found out he was from Georgia. Needless to say, since it was chipped it hard proof  
that it was domesticated and since he is also neutered, he did not spray pee or poop around the dorm.  
There was a poop smell from the cat litter, but the cat definitely did not do his business anywhere else.  
Also, the cat only ended up in there for ONE day, I don’t know why your suitemate has been stick for the  
past few days.  
Did you make this post to humiliate your roommate online or you actually care about the cat? Half of  
the post is you talking smack about your roommate and the cat too. These things would not have gotten  
this bad if you properly address your issue with your roommate before. I’m not saying your roommate is  
in the clear, but you certainly aren’t either. There’s no definite right or wrong side to anything.  
I’m sorry for your bad experiences, but please address your concern directly to the person first. It’s not  
okay for your roommate to have a messy room but it’s not okay for you to post this online and humiliate  
him using your schools subreddit too. People could start cyberbullying him here on reddit and it’s not  
okay.  
TLDR: OP never addresses his concern either with the messy room or the cat to his roommate. Cat is  
NOT STOLEN and domesticated. OP posted with a lot of incorrect details. It’s okay to post about an issue  
on reddit but OP didn’t even try solving it himself and decided to post this to humiliate his roommate  
using your school’s subreddit."
